sources.entry: hemanth/functional-programming-jargon: jargon from the functional programming world in simple terms

summary.one_liner: A glossary of functional programming terms, each explained with short JavaScript examples, for people learning FP.
summary.what_it_does: The README is an alphabetical-style glossary of functional programming jargon, with a table of contents covering terms such as arity, closures, currying, function composition, monads, functors, applicative functors, morphisms, and optics (lenses, prisms, isos, traversals). Each entry gives a plain-language definition followed by a short JavaScript (ES2015) code sample, and many entries link to further reading. It also lists translations of the document into many languages and points to an interactive graph version. The README is truncated, so the final entries (such as type signatures, Option, Either, and partial/total functions) are not fully visible here.
use_cases: looking up the meaning of an FP term like monad or functor
studying functional concepts with JavaScript examples
reference for explaining FP jargon to teammates
finding translated FP glossaries in other languages
notable: Examples written in JavaScript, with a note on why JavaScript was chosen
Terms aligned with the Fantasy Land spec where applicable
Available in many translations, including Portuguese, Spanish, Chinese, Korean, and French
Covers advanced topics like free monads, profunctors, and optics alongside basics
Links to an interactive graph version of the glossary
caveats: README is truncated, so some later sections are not fully visible
Examples are in JavaScript only, not a general FP tutorial
License not stated in the provided README excerpt
